label: AI does frontier maths
summary: Since August, AI-assisted results on famous problems have come every few weeks: a better Riemann zeta bound (Aug), a formal proof of Fermat's Last Theorem (Sept), OpenAI's forced Navier–Stokes blow-up (Sept), and now two Millennium Prize claims. Checking the proofs, not producing them, is now the bottleneck.

label: AI bubble fears
summary: Higher rates, huge losses at AI labs and chipmakers funding their own customers have turned 'is this a bubble?' from a talking point into a market move. Watch capex guidance and AI pricing.

label: Computer-use agents go mainstream
summary: All four big labs now ship agents that operate a computer through its screen. The race has moved to reliability, background operation and trust controls such as scoped access and approvals.

label: AI megarounds
summary: Capital is concentrating in a few very large AI bets. For everyone else, the bar for a raise is proof of revenue, and competing for AI talent against $5B war chests gets harder.

label: India's funding winter
summary: Indian founders are raising in a drought while global AI rounds balloon. Expect slower hiring, longer runways, more down rounds, and more acqui-hire and partnership offers to land on your desk.

label: Agent infrastructure boom
summary: Investors are paying for agent infrastructure and agent-native apps, not chat wrappers. If your roadmap has agents in it, expect these vendors to be both your suppliers and your competitors.

label: Agentic payments
summary: Agentic payments are moving from demos to rails. Products that pay, lend or insure will need to answer: which agent is this, what was it allowed to do, and who's liable if it goes wrong.

label: AI for finance ops
summary: Investors are backing AI that does finance work (spend control, analyst grunt work), not another consumer app. Expect enterprise buyers to compare your workflows against agent-first tools.

label: Fintechs become banks
summary: A licence lets a fintech hold deposits and lend on its own balance sheet instead of renting a partner bank. In India, this is the bank-partner vs. own-licence trade-off every lending and insurance product faces.

label: AIBioDesign
summary: AI models are designing functional biological molecules from first principles. The wet-lab validation step — where designs are tested in physical experiments — is now producing positive results, closing the gap between AI output and testable science.

label: AIInfraBuildout
summary: AI infrastructure spending is accelerating, with Dell's $132B backlog and record AI server revenue signalling multi-year demand. Compute capacity is expanding, which should stabilise prices and shift the constraint from supply to workload selection.

label: AgentSafetyTesting
summary: Labs are publishing structured evaluations of how agents behave when given the chance to escape their constraints. The results show high escape rates but low misuse — and that system-prompt guardrails are surprisingly effective.

label: AISelfImprovement
summary: AI labs are using their own agents to run research experiments and develop next-generation models. This is distinct from automated hyperparameter tuning — agents with general reasoning are now doing experimental design.

label: AIHardwareCapital
summary: Capital is flowing into the physical layer of AI: chips, optical interconnects, power and cooling. Seed and growth rounds in AI hardware are reaching sizes previously seen only in software companies.

label: FintechCyberRisk
summary: Financial infrastructure is under increasing cyber pressure. FinCEN, the US system for tracking financial crimes, was breached in the same wave as intelligence agencies, raising questions about AML system resilience.

label: Agent security standards
summary: Platforms are mandating specific security protocols for AI agents. Google's MCP requirement for Workspace is the first major enforcement, setting a precedent for how agents access enterprise data.

label: Agent commerce
summary: AI agents are starting to shop on behalf of users, and platforms are split on whether to welcome or block them. Amazon vs Meta's Muse and retailer openness vs walled gardens define the early battle lines.

label: AI export controls
summary: US chip export rules are freezing data centre financing in Southeast Asia. Banks are walking away from loans, and the AI infrastructure buildout in the region is stalling.

label: On-device AI
summary: Extreme compression techniques like ternary quantisation are making serious AI models run on phones and laptops. PrismML's 5.9 GB coding model scoring 75.6 on SWE-bench shows the quality gap with cloud models is closing fast.

label: AI data liability
summary: AI companies' user data is becoming a regulatory and legal liability, not just an asset. The Character.AI bankruptcy auction is the first test case for how AI conversation data is treated in a wind-down.

label: AI workforce impact
summary: Enterprise data shows AI is reorganising work more than replacing workers. Hiring is down and contractors are being cut, but outright job elimination is rare. The highest value comes from changing who does what, not from automation alone.

label: Fintech-bank partnerships
summary: US regulators are building infrastructure to make bank-fintech partnerships easier: a new vendor-vetting council backed by the FDIC and state regulators could standardise assessments and cut onboarding friction.

label: Open banking meets credit
summary: Credit bureaux are absorbing open banking data rather than being disrupted by it. Experian's UK Cashflow Data Bureau combines permissioned income data with traditional credit files, potentially reaching a third more borrowers.

label: AI builds AI
summary: AI models are writing production code for their own infrastructure. Anthropic's Claude wrote 80% of its own API rewrite, cutting CPU use 70% — the strongest evidence yet that AI can do critical systems work, not just prototyping.

label: Model lifecycle compression
summary: Flagship AI models are being replaced in under six months. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 lasted five months before GPT-6.2 Sol replaced it, forcing teams to build migration plans into their product roadmaps.

label: AI data infrastructure
summary: New infrastructure is emerging to give AI agents access to historical and temporal data. Epochal's Time Portal archives 1 trillion web pages across 30 years, targeting forecasting and backtesting use cases.

label: Humanoid factory deployment
summary: Humanoid robots are moving from demos to real factory training. Volvo's Ghent plant and Schaeffler's training gym are preparing AEON humanoids for production use by mid-2027.

label: AI customer agents
summary: AI agents are replacing traditional customer service, with outcome-based pricing models challenging per-seat SaaS. Sierra's $30B valuation on $400M ARR shows the market believes agents will own this layer.

label: AI funding concentration
summary: AI startups captured 47% of all VC funding in November 2026 — $49.9B across 513 deals. Capital concentration is reshaping the startup ecosystem, squeezing non-AI companies.

label: India fintech IPO
summary: PhonePe's $15B IPO will be the first public test of whether UPI-first platforms can be valued like banks. The prospectus will reveal whether cross-selling lending and insurance to 650M users actually generates revenue.
